newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Grinaker, Wilson Bayly to build casino.
newsitem.headline: Grinaker, Wilson Bayly to build casino.

text.p: South African gaming consortium Global Resorts said on Wednesday it had awarded a 90 million rand construction contract to firms Grinaker Building Inland and Wilson Bayly Holmes Ovcon Ltd.
Managing director Ernie Joubert told Reuters the companies would build a casino complex in Mpumalanga province for Global, which in May won one of the provinces three gaming licences.
"We didn't put out a tender. We negotiated a price because only few companies can do this kind of work. We (went) directly to the ones who can do the work," Joubert said.
Grinaker Building Inland is a division of construction firm Grinaker Construction Ltd -- part of the greater construction to electronics Grinaker group.
He said that the total investment capital in the 17,000 square-metre complex was 200 million rand.
"Those two companies have the building contract which comes to the region of about 90 million rand," Joubert said.
He said that construction was scheduled to be completed next August. A temporary casino would start operating from November this year.
Legislation passed last year legalised casino gaming in South Africa for the first time and gave control of the running of the industry to the country's nine provinces.
Joubert said that among the complex's features would be a golf course a hotel, tennis courts, a conference centre and restaurants.
Global Resorts shareholders include South Africa's Genbel Securities Ltd and Rand Merchant Bank, which is owned by RMB Holdings Ltd.
Mpumalanga awarded two other casino licenses to Tsogo Sun Holdings, a joint-venture between a black consortium and South African Breweries' hotels unit Southern Sun.
